why: This week is Simulation + Strings. Walk the message, count consonants only, and on every n-th one substitute the next consonant from the 21-letter consonant alphabet, keeping case and wrapping z to b.
hints: Vowels and non-letters do not advance the consonant counter.
Build a map from each consonant to the next one in 'bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz', cyclically, so z maps to b. Apply it to the lowercase letter and restore the case.
One pass with a counter: when count % n == 0, replace. Collect the pieces in a list and join them. O(len).
pitfalls: The next consonant skips vowels: 'd' becomes 'f', not 'e'.
Keep the case: 'S' becomes 'T' and 'Z' becomes 'B'.
Count consonants regardless of case: 'C' and 'c' both count.
statement:
Given a string message and an integer n, replace every n-th consonant (counting only consonants, from the left) with the next consonant in alphabetical order, keeping its case. The consonant order is b c d f g h j k l m n p q r s t v w x y z, and z/Z wraps around to b/B. Vowels (a, e, i, o, u) and any other characters stay unchanged and are not counted.

Example: message = "CodeSignal", n = 3.

  • Consonants in order: C(1), d(2), S(3), g(4), n(5), l(6).
  • The 3rd is S, which becomes T. The 6th is l, which becomes m.
  • Result: "CodeTignam".
constraints: • Not stated in the source (it only allows up to O(message.length²)). Assume 1 ≤ message.length ≤ 104, 1 ≤ n ≤ 104, and that message contains English letters and possibly other printable characters.
